mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the form "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have".
mathgap.example: Treating the phrase as an absolute difference or swapping the order of terms.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement says "X has N items" (or similar).
mathgap.example: Ignoring later transfers and treating the count as final.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more items than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer items than Y" as X = Y - N.
mathgap.example: Reversing the sign of the offset.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, give each recipient half of the original person's items and set the original's count to zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrase "splits all" and names two recipients.
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full amount instead of half, or forgetting to zero the original.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement says "X gives N items to Y".
mathgap.example: Applying a transfer out of order or using stale counts.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known, substitute its numeric value into the equation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving a signed‑difference equality and one side is already determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known difference as a symbolic term instead of plugging in its value.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given, updating counts after each step; later statements refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any problem where statements can affect each other's values.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a later statement that should see the effect of earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Preserve order in signed difference statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions the "difference between X and Y", treat it as the signed difference X − Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrase "difference between X and Y".
mathgap.example: Swapping X and Y and thus changing the sign of the difference.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: When a conditional transfer statement appears (e.g., "If X has more than N apples, X will transfer t ..."), handle the condition appropriately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer is guarded by a condition.
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer regardless of whether the condition holds.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of equations needed to solve for the target variable by tracing dependencies from the target through the statements, and ignore unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a problem contains many statements, but only a subset involve the target variable directly or indirectly.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations, including many unrelated statements, instead of focusing on the equations that involve the target variable.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may misinterpret the phrase "difference between X and Y" as an absolute value or reverse the order, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always treat "difference between X and Y" as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order given.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may apply transfers out of order, using outdated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements in the order they appear, updating counts immediately.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat a direct count assignment as the final value, ignoring later transfers that modify it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct count assignments as the current count at that point, and continue to apply any subsequent transfers.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may overlook the condition and always apply the transfer.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Check the condition before applying a conditional transfer; only apply if the condition holds.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting "increase by a/b times" as additive rather than multiplicative
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may read "increase by a/b times" as adding a/b to the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret "increase by a/b times" as multiplying the current count by (a/b).
